local.heading: Apex keeps adding neighbors who have never heard of your business.
paragraphs: Apex got its name from the railroad. When the Chatham Railroad was finished in 1869, the highest point on the line sat right here, and workers called it the apex of the grade. The town incorporated in 1873. A fire in 1911 burned most of the downtown business district, and the brick blocks rebuilt after it still stand, which is why the downtown is counted among the most intact railroad towns in the state.

The growth since then is the part that matters for marketing. Apex's population quadrupled during the 1990s and has kept climbing. With growth like that, a lot of households in town are new to it, from Green Level and Friendship out to New Hill. A new arrival has no neighbor list to lean on. They search on a phone, compare reviews, and call whichever company looks local and trustworthy.

Getting around shapes the market too. NC 540, US 1, US 64, and NC 55 all run through town, with Research Triangle Park just north, Cary along the north and east, and Holly Springs to the south. That puts Cary and Raleigh businesses in the same search results as yours. Local employers include Dell, Apex Tool Group, ATI Industrial Automation, Bland Landscaping, and Costco, along with Wake County Public Schools and the Town of Apex itself.

More is coming. RXR is building Veridea, a 1,100-acre mixed-use community between NC 55 and I-540, and NC Children's, a UNC Health and Duke Health partnership, picked a 230-acre site inside it for a freestanding children's hospital. Downtown, Salem Street went into a streetscape rebuild in January 2026. More rooftops and more competition mean the businesses with clear, current websites tend to get the first call.

industries.heading: Apex businesses we build for
industries.intro: Apex is mostly families, commuters, and a lot of new construction. These are the businesses that win or lose on local search here.

items.name: Contractors and home services for new subdivisions
items.body: Landscapers, fence builders, pool companies, HVAC, and handymen serving neighborhoods out toward Green Level and New Hill. Pages that name the communities you work in, plus photos of real jobs, help a new homeowner pick you.

items.name: Salem Street shops and restaurants
items.body: Downtown storefronts that live on weekend foot traffic, PeakFest crowds, and holiday events. With the streetscape work going on, the site and Google profile need current hours, parking help, and directions.

items.name: Medical, dental, and therapy practices
items.body: Family doctors, pediatric dentists, orthodontists, and physical therapists serving young families. Parents compare offices on their phone, so insurance, location, and online booking need to be easy to find.

items.name: Childcare, tutoring, and youth activities
items.body: Preschools, learning centers, dance studios, and sports programs. Parents want schedules, age groups, pricing, and a sign-up form, and they will move on fast if they can't find them.

items.name: Professional services for commuters
items.body: Accountants, insurance agents, real estate teams, and financial planners whose clients work in RTP or Raleigh. The site has to look polished and make booking a call quick for someone with a busy schedule.

howWeWork.heading: How we work with Apex businesses
paragraphs: Creative Cowboys is Josh and Dave, based in Villa Rica, Georgia, west of Atlanta. We don't keep an office in the Triangle, so Apex projects run on video calls and shared drafts. We learn how your business works, send a clickable draft of the site, and keep adjusting it from your feedback until it fits.

You won't get handed off to an account rep. The same two people who build the site write your area pages and handle the SEO every month after launch. If coming up to see your shop or jobsite would make the work better, we'll plan the trip.

faqs.q: How much does web design in Apex, NC cost?
faqs.a: Most Apex businesses start on our Local Marketing Package: $297 a month, month to month, no contract. It includes local SEO, paid ads management if you want ads (your ad budget is separate), and a custom website valued at $3,500 at no extra cost.

faqs.q: Can an Apex business compete with Cary and Raleigh companies in search?
faqs.a: For people searching in and around Apex, often yes. Google weighs location heavily on local searches. A site that clearly names the town and the areas you serve, a complete Google profile, and steady reviews from local customers give you a real shot against bigger firms that only mention Raleigh.

faqs.q: Should my site have pages for Green Level or Holly Springs?
faqs.a: Only if you take work there. A page for each area you really serve helps you show up in those searches. We skip places you don't cover, because those pages bring in calls you can't use and Google tends to ignore them.

faqs.q: My shop is on Salem Street. What should the website focus on?
faqs.a: Accurate hours, directions, parking notes, and photos that show what's inside. During the streetscape work, it helps to post updates on how to reach you. We keep the site and your Google profile in sync so visitors aren't confused.

faqs.q: Do we need to meet in person?
faqs.a: No. We're in Villa Rica, Georgia, and almost all of the work happens over video calls and drafts you review on your phone. If an in-person visit would help the project, we'll set one up.

faqs.q: How long does a new website take to launch?
faqs.a: Most sites go live in a few weeks. The timeline depends mostly on how fast we get your photos, service details, and feedback on the draft. Local SEO starts at the same time, so the site launches ready to be found.
